author: Tsuchiya Yuto <kitakar@gmail.com>
subject: (surface3-oemb) add DMI matches for Surface 3 with broken DMI table
message:
On some Surface 3, the DMI table gets corrupted for unknown reasons
and breaks existing DMI matching used for device-specific quirks.

This commit adds the (broken) DMI data into dmi_system_id tables used
for quirks so that each driver can enable quirks even on the affected
systems.

On affected systems, DMI data will look like this:
    $ grep . /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/{bios_vendor,board_name,board_vendor,\
    chassis_vendor,product_name,sys_vendor}
    /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/bios_vendor:American Megatrends Inc.
    /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/board_name:OEMB
    /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/board_vendor:OEMB
    /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/chassis_vendor:OEMB
    /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/product_name:OEMB
    /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/sys_vendor:OEMB

Expected:
    $ grep . /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/{bios_vendor,board_name,board_vendor,\
    chassis_vendor,product_name,sys_vendor}
    /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/bios_vendor:American Megatrends Inc.
    /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/board_name:Surface 3
    /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/board_vendor:Microsoft Corporation
    /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/chassis_vendor:Microsoft Corporation
    /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/product_name:Surface 3
    /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/sys_vendor:Microsoft Corporation

author: kitakar5525 <34676735+kitakar5525@users.noreply.github.com>
subject: surface3-spi: workaround: disable DMA mode to avoid crash by default
message:
On Arch Linux kernel at least after 4.19, touch input is broken after suspend
(s2idle).

        kern  :err   : [  +0.203408] Surface3-spi spi-MSHW0037:00: SPI transfer timed out

On recent stable Arch Linux kernel (at least after 5.1), touch input will
crash after the first touch.

        kern  :err   : [  +0.203592] Surface3-spi spi-MSHW0037:00: SPI transfer timed out
        kern  :err   : [  +0.000173] spi_master spi1: failed to transfer one message from queue

I found on an affected system (Arch Linux kernel, etc.), the touchscreen
driver uses DMA mode by default. Then, we found some kernels with different
kernel config (5.1 kernel config from Jakeday [1] or Chromium OS kernel
chromeos-4.19 [2]) will use PIO mode by default and no such issues there.

So, this commit disables DMA mode on the touchscreen driver side as a quick
workaround to avoid touch input crash.
We may need to properly set up DMA mode to use the touchscreen driver with
DMA mode.

You can still switch DMA/PIO mode if you want:

  switch to DMA mode (maybe broken)
        echo 1 | sudo tee /sys/module/surface3_spi/parameters/use_dma
  back to PIO mode
        echo 0 | sudo tee /sys/module/surface3_spi/parameters/use_dma

Link to issue: https://github.com/jakeday/linux-surface/issues/596

References:
[1] https://github.com/jakeday/linux-surface/blob/master/configs/5.1/config
[2] https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromiumos/third_party/kernel/+/refs/heads/chromeos-4.19

Tested on Arch Linux 5.4.1 with Surf

  symbol 'use_dma' was not declared. Should it be static?

Make it static and drop the redundant zero initialiser. No functional

This fixes the patch "surface3-spi: workaround: disable DMA mode to
avoid crash by default" in the surface3 patchset.

author: =?UTF-8?q?Jonas=20Dre=C3=9Fler?= <verdre@v0yd.nl>
subject: mwifiex: Add quirk resetting the PCI bridge on MS Surface devices
message:
The most recent firmware of the 88W8897 card reports a hardcoded LTR
value to the system during initialization, probably as an (unsuccessful)
attempt of the developers to fix firmware crashes. This LTR value
prevents most of the Microsoft Surface devices from entering deep
powersaving states (either platform C-State 10 or S0ix state), because
the exit latency of that state would be higher than what the card can
tolerate.

Turns out the card works just the same (including the firmware crashes)
no matter if that hardcoded LTR value is reported or not, so it's kind
of useless and only prevents us from saving power.

To get rid of those hardcoded LTR reports, it's possible to reset the
PCI bridge device after initializing the cards firmware. I'm not exactly
sure why that works, maybe the power management subsystem of the PCH
resets its stored LTR values when doing a function level reset of the
bridge device. Doing the reset once after starting the wifi firmware
works very well, probably because the firmware only reports that LTR
value a single time during firmware startup.

Patchset: mwifiex

author: Tsuchiya Yuto <kitakar@gmail.com>
subject: mwifiex: pcie: disable bridge_d3 for Surface gen4+
message:
Currently, mwifiex fw will crash after suspend on recent kernel series.
On Windows, it seems that the root port of wifi will never enter D3 state
(stay on D0 state). And on Linux, disabling the D3 state for the
bridge fixes fw crashing after suspend.

This commit disables the D3 state of root port on driver initialization
and fixes fw crashing after suspend.

Signed-off-by: Tsuchiya Yuto <kitakar@gmail.com>
Patchset: mwifiex

author: =?UTF-8?q?Jonas=20Dre=C3=9Fler?= <verdre@v0yd.nl>
subject: Bluetooth: btusb: Lower passive lescan interval on Marvell 88W8897
message:
The Marvell 88W8897 combined wifi and bluetooth card (pcie+usb version)
is used in a lot of Microsoft Surface devices, and all those devices
suffer from very low 2.4GHz wifi connection speeds while bluetooth is
enabled. The reason for that is that the default passive scanning
interval for Bluetooth Low Energy devices is quite high in Linux
(interval of 60 msec and scan window of 30 msec, see hci_core.c), and
the Marvell chip is known for its bad bt+wifi coexisting performance.

So decrease that passive scan interval and make the scan window shorter
on this particular device to allow for spending more time transmitting
wifi signals: The new scan interval is 250 msec (0x190 * 0.625 msec) and
the new scan window is 6.25 msec (0xa * 0,625 msec).

This change has a very large impact on the 2.4GHz wifi speeds and gets
it up to performance comparable with the Windows driver, which seems to
apply a similar quirk.

The interval and window length were tested and found to work very well
with a lot of Bluetooth Low Energy devices, including the Surface Pen, a
Bluetooth Speaker and two modern Bluetooth headphones. All devices were
discovered immediately after turning them on. Even lower values were
also tested, but they introduced longer delays until devices get
discovered.

Patchset: mwifiex

author: Anthony Lee <108008609+orthogonaleety@users.noreply.github.com>
subject: hid: ipts: Fix size of synthesized HID data report
message:
IPTS_HID_REPORT_DATA_SIZE is passed to hid_input_report() as the size of
the synthesized data report. It does not account for the report ID (1
byte) and the scan time field (2 bytes) declared in the fallback HID
descriptor, i.e. the report is 3 bytes shorter than the descriptor says.

Since commit 0a3fe972a7cb ("HID: core: Mitigate potential OOB by
removing bogus memset()"), hid-core drops reports that are shorter than
expected instead of padding them, which breaks touch input on devices
using the fallback descriptor (e.g. Surface Book 1).

Fix this by including the report ID and scan time in the report size.

Link: https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/2150
Link: https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/pull/2233

author: Wu Enqiang <janussss@163.com>
subject: surface: aggregator: propagate -EPROBE_DEFER from ssam_irq_setup()
message:
gpiod_get() can fail with -EPROBE_DEFER when the GPIO controller
providing the "ssam_wakeup-int" GPIO has not been probed yet. The
current error path falls back to fwnode_irq_get(), which returns
-EINVAL because this device only declares GPIO resources. The probe
then fails hard and is never retried.

This has been reported across various Surface devices since v6.12,
including the Pro 6 and Pro 9 that were used to reproduce it. With
the SSAM controller down, dependent ACPI devices, e.g. the battery
with its _DEP on the SAN node, are never enumerated and battery
status is missing.

Use gpiod_get_optional() and propagate errors to the caller so that
probing is deferred until the GPIO controller becomes available. Only
when no wakeup GPIO is described at all, fall back to fwnode_irq_get().

Fixes: b27622f13172 ("platform/surface: Add OF support")
Reported-by: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/platform-driver-x86/d0bb21cc-6d3c-4526-8204-2511da51a6ac@nilk.net
Link: https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/2219
Tested-by: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
Tested-by: Wu Enqiang <janussss@163.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Wu Enqiang <janussss@163.com>
Link: https://patchwork.kernel.org/project/platform-driver-x86/patch/20261024054921.48209-1-janussss@163.com/
Patchset: surface-sam

author: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
subject: power: supply: surface_battery: Report not charging while idle on AC
message:
While the EC holds the charge level below full, the battery is idle and
the adapter powers the device, but the battery keeps reporting a small
rate that is not always zero, and the discharging bit is sometimes set.
Status then flickers between "Not charging", "Unknown" and "Discharging"
with the adapter online.

On a Surface Pro 9 held at 78% on AC, reads one to two seconds apart
returned all three statuses. Over six minutes, half of it under full CPU
load, the rate stayed under 100 mW apart from two spikes of two seconds,
at most 671 mW. Idle reads in the same session reached 953 mW. The
capacity did not move.

When the rate is at most 1000 mW, ask the EC for the power source. If it
is the adapter, report not charging, regardless of the discharging bit.
A larger rate is reported as before. Charging, and full with no state bit
set, are unchanged, but a small rate with the discharging bit set now
reports not charging when full, or when the charging bit is also set.

A real drain below 1000 mW on an adapter too weak for the load therefore
reads as not charging. So that low battery warnings still work, the rule
is off below 20% capacity, when the battery reports critical, or when the
capacity is not known. It is also off on devices reporting in mA, as the
cutoff is a power.

The request goes directly to the EC, as a read through the adapter's power
supply can consume its change notification. It uses the adapter's target
and instance on all devices. The readings above are from be

author: Maximilian Luz <luzmaximilian@gmail.com>
subject: i2c: acpi: Implement RawBytes read access
message:
Microsoft Surface Pro 4 and Book 1 devices access the MSHW0030 I2C
device via a generic serial bus operation region and RawBytes read
access. On the Surface Book 1, this access is required to turn on (and
off) the discrete GPU.

Multiple things are to note here:

a) The RawBytes access is device/driver dependent. The ACPI
   specification states:

   > Raw accesses assume that the writer has knowledge of the bus that
   > the access is made over and the device that is being accessed. The
   > protocol may only ensure that the buffer is transmitted to the
   > appropriate driver, but the driver must be able to interpret the
   > buffer to communicate to a register.

   Thus this implementation may likely not work on other devices
   accessing I2C via the RawBytes accessor type.

b) The MSHW0030 I2C device is an HID-over-I2C device which seems to
   serve multiple functions:

   1. It is the main access point for the legacy-type Surface Aggregator
      Module (also referred to as SAM-over-HID, as opposed to the newer
      SAM-over-SSH/UART). It has currently not been determined on how
      support for the legacy SAM should be implemented. Likely via a
      custom HID driver.

   2. It seems to serve as the HID device for the Integrated Sensor Hub.
      This might complicate matters with regards to implementing a
      SAM-over-HID driver required by legacy SAM.

In light of this, the simplest approach has been chosen for now.
However, it may make more sense regarding break

author: Maximilian Luz <luzmaximilian@gmail.com>
subject: platform/surface: Add driver for Surface Book 1 dGPU switch
message:
Add driver exposing the discrete GPU power-switch of the  Microsoft
Surface Book 1 to user-space.

On the Surface Book 1, the dGPU power is controlled via the Surface
System Aggregator Module (SAM). The specific SAM-over-HID command for
this is exposed via ACPI. This module provides a simple driver exposing
the ACPI call via a sysfs parameter to user-space, so that users can
easily power-on/-off the dGPU.

author: Maximilian Luz <luzmaximilian@gmail.com>
subject: USB: quirks: Add USB_QUIRK_DELAY_INIT for Surface Go 3 Type-Cover
message:
The touchpad on the Type-Cover of the Surface Go 3 is sometimes not
being initialized properly. Apply USB_QUIRK_DELAY_INIT to fix this
issue.

More specifically, the device in question is a fairly standard modern
touchpad with pointer and touchpad input modes. During setup, the device
needs to be switched from pointer- to touchpad-mode (which is done in
hid-multitouch) to fully utilize it as intended. Unfortunately, however,
this seems to occasionally fail silently, leaving the device in
pointer-mode. Applying USB_QUIRK_DELAY_INIT seems to fix this.

Link: https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/1059
Signed-off-by: Maximilian Luz <luzmaximilian@gmail.com>
Patchset: surface-typecover

author: =?UTF-8?q?Jonas=20Dre=C3=9Fler?= <verdre@v0yd.nl>
subject: hid/multitouch: Turn off Type Cover keyboard backlight when suspending
message:
The Type Cover for Microsoft Surface devices supports a special usb
control request to disable or enable the built-in keyboard backlight.
On Windows, this request happens when putting the device into suspend or
resuming it, without it the backlight of the Type Cover will remain
enabled for some time even though the computer is suspended, which looks
weird to the user.

So add support for this special usb control request to hid-multitouch,
which is the driver that's handling the Type Cover.

The reason we have to use a pm_notifier for this instead of the usual
suspend/resume methods is that those won't get called in case the usb
device is already autosuspended.

Also, if the device is autosuspended, we have to briefly autoresume it
in order to send the request. Doing that should be fine, the usb-core
driver does something similar during suspend inside choose_wakeup().

To make sure we don't send that request to every device but only to
devices which support it, add a new quirk
MT_CLS_WIN_8_MS_SURFACE_TYPE_COVER to hid-multitouch. For now this quirk
is only enabled for the usb id of the Surface Pro 2017 Type Cover, which
is where I confirmed that it's working.

Patchset: surface-typecover

author: PJungkamp <p.jungkamp@gmail.com>
subject: hid/multitouch: Add support for surface pro type cover tablet switch
message:
The Surface Pro Type Cover has several non standard HID usages in it's
hid report descriptor.
I noticed that, upon folding the typecover back, a vendor specific range
of 4 32 bit integer hid usages is transmitted.
Only the first byte of the message seems to convey reliable information
about the keyboard state.

0x22 => Normal (keys enabled)
0x33 => Folded back (keys disabled)
0x53 => Rotated left/right side up (keys disabled)
0x13 => Cover closed (keys disabled)
0x43 => Folded back and Tablet upside down (keys disabled)
This list may not be exhaustive.

The tablet mode switch will be disabled for a value of 0x22 and enabled
on any other value.

Patchset: surface-typecover

author: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
subject: hid/multitouch: Register Type Cover PM notifier after starting the device
message:
mt_probe() registers td->pm_notifier for the Type Cover keyboard
backlight before parsing the report descriptor. This has two problems:

- The Apple Touch Bar check returns -ENODEV without unregistering the
  notifier. td is devm-allocated, so it is freed while the notifier is
  still on the PM notifier chain, and the next suspend calls into freed
  memory.

- A suspend during probe can run the notifier before hid_hw_start(), so
  update_keyboard_backlight() would send a request to a device that has
  not been started.

Register the notifier only after hid_hw_start() has succeeded. Every
exit path after that point returns success, so mt_remove() always
unregisters it, and the error-path unregisters are no longer needed.
The notifier itself still checks the backlight quirk at run time, so
behaviour on working devices is unchanged.

This fixes the patch "hid/multitouch: Turn off Type Cover keyboard
backlight when suspending" in the surface-typecover patchset.

Signed-off-by: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
Patchset: surface-typecover

author: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
subject: hid/multitouch: Only toggle Type Cover backlight on USB devices
message:
The Surface Type Cover entry in the device table matches the device ID
on any bus, but update_keyboard_backlight() unconditionally treats the
device as USB and uses hid_to_usb_dev(). For a non-USB device with the
same IDs, this treats whatever sits two levels up in the device
hierarchy as a usb_device on every suspend and resume: an unrelated
device for transports such as I2C, or a NULL pointer for uhid.

Return early unless the device is on USB, as other HID drivers do with
hid_is_usb(). hid_is_usb() is provided by usbhid, which hid-multitouch
did not depend on before, so only call it when usbhid is reachable.
When hid-multitouch is built in and usbhid is a module, the backlight is
left alone instead of failing to link. When both are modules,
hid-multitouch now depends on usbhid, like other HID drivers using
hid_is_usb().

This fixes the patch "hid/multitouch: Turn off Type Cover keyboard
backlight when suspending" in the surface-typecover patchset.

Signed-off-by: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
Patchset: surface-typecover

author: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
subject: hid/multitouch: Add missing NULL checks to Type Cover tablet switch
message:
The Type Cover tablet-mode switch code dereferences pointers that the
surrounding code treats as optional:

- mt_input_mapped() and mt_event() check rdata for NULL before using it
  for multitouch collections, but the tablet-mode switch check that
  follows reads rdata->application unconditionally.
  mt_find_report_data() returns NULL if allocating the report data or
  its application fails.

- mt_event() and mt_remove() use field->hidinput->input without a
  check, although hid-input clears field->hidinput when it drops an
  input device without capabilities, and other code in this driver
  checks it.

Check both before use.

This fixes the patch "hid/multitouch: Add support for surface pro type
cover tablet switch" in the surface-typecover patchset.

Signed-off-by: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
Patchset: surface-typecover

author: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
subject: hid/multitouch: Write Type Cover backlight value by usage index
message:
update_keyboard_backlight() stores the new backlight state in
field->value[field->index]. field->index is the field's position within
its report, not a position in the field's value array, so for a report
in which the backlight field is not the first field this writes the
wrong value, and if the index is beyond the field's values it writes
outside the value array. The report descriptor comes from the device,
so a device claiming the Type Cover IDs controls both.

Look up the value slot of the backlight usage and check it against the
field's report count before writing. When the backlight usage is the
first usage of the first field in its report, the written slot is the
same as before. This has not been tested on a Type Cover with these
IDs.

This fixes the patch "hid/multitouch: Turn off Type Cover keyboard
backlight when suspending" in the surface-typecover patchset.

Signed-off-by: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
Patchset: surface-typecover

author: Maximilian Luz <luzmaximilian@gmail.com>
subject: PCI: Add quirk to prevent calling shutdown method

author: Hans de Goede <hdegoede@redhat.com>
subject: ACPI: delay enumeration of devices with a _DEP pointing to an INT3472 device
message:
The clk and regulator frameworks expect clk/regulator consumer-devices
to have info about the consumed clks/regulators described in the device's
fw_node.

To work around cases where this info is not present in the firmware tables,
which is often the case on x86/ACPI devices, both frameworks allow the
provider-driver to attach info about consumers to the clks/regulators
when registering these.

This causes problems with the probe ordering wrt drivers for consumers
of these clks/regulators. Since the lookups are only registered when the
provider-driver binds, trying to get these clks/regulators before then
results in a -ENOENT error for clks and a dummy regulator for regulators.

One case where we hit this issue is camera sensors such as e.g. the OV8865
sensor found on the Microsoft Surface Go. The sensor uses clks, regulators
and GPIOs provided by a TPS68470 PMIC which is described in an INT3472
ACPI device. There is special platform code handling this and setting
platform_data with the necessary consumer info on the MFD cells
instantiated for the PMIC under: drivers/platform/x86/intel/int3472.

For this to work properly the ov8865 driver must not bind to the I2C-client
for the OV8865 sensor until after the TPS68470 PMIC gpio, regulator and
clk MFD cells have all been fully setup.

The OV8865 on the Microsoft Surface Go is just one example, all X86
devices using the Intel IPU3 camera block found on recent Intel SoCs
have similar issues where there is an INT3472 HID ACPI-device

author: zouxiaoh <xiaohong.zou@intel.com>
subject: iommu: intel-ipu: use IOMMU passthrough mode for Intel IPUs
message:
Intel IPU(Image Processing Unit) has its own (IO)MMU hardware,
The IPU driver allocates its own page table that is not mapped
via the DMA, and thus the Intel IOMMU driver blocks access giving
this error: DMAR: DRHD: handling fault status reg 3 DMAR:
[DMA Read] Request device [00:05.0] PASID ffffffff
fault addr 76406000 [fault reason 06] PTE Read access is not set
As IPU is not an external facing device which is not risky, so use
IOMMU passthrough mode for Intel IPUs.

author: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
subject: media: v4l2-core: Release privacy LED when registration fails
message:
Acquiring the privacy LED was moved from
__v4l2_async_register_subdev_sensor() into
__v4l2_async_register_subdev(), but the matching release on failure was
left in the sensor wrapper. As a result, sub-devices registered directly
with v4l2_async_register_subdev() keep the LED reference, and the LED's
sysfs interface stays disabled, when registration fails.

Release the LED on the error paths of the function that acquires it,
and drop the release from the sensor wrapper, which would otherwise
release it a second time. v4l2-fwnode.c no longer uses the private
privacy LED helpers, so drop its include of v4l2-subdev-priv.h.

This fixes the patch "media: v4l2-core: Acquire privacy led in
v4l2_async_register_subdev()" in the cameras patchset.

author: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
subject: media: v4l2-core: Only look up privacy LED for sub-devices with a device
message:
Acquiring the privacy LED was moved from
__v4l2_async_register_subdev_sensor(), which rejects sub-devices without
a struct device, into __v4l2_async_register_subdev(), which treats
sd->dev as optional. The lookup goes through led_get(sd->dev, ...),
which dereferences the device, so registering a sub-device without one
would crash.

Only look up the LED when the sub-device has a device. Without one,
sd->privacy_led stays NULL and the release paths do nothing.

This fixes the patch "media: v4l2-core: Acquire privacy led in
v4l2_async_register_subdev()" in the cameras patchset.

author: Fernando Rimoli <fernandorimoli11@gmail.com>
subject: media: i2c: ov5693: Gate the MIPI clock lane for non-continuous clock

Tested-by: Jakob Berg Jespersen <dev@berg.pm> # Surface Pro 7+, IPU6 Tiger Lake
Fil Dunsky <filipp.dunsky@gmail.com> # Surface Pro 8, IPU6 Tiger Lake (8086:9a19)
Lucas Lis <lucaseze.lis@gmail.com> # Surface Pro 7+, IPU6 Tiger Lake (0x9a19)
Kengo Oki <dev.kengo.fugu0141@gmail.com> # Surface Go 4, IPU6 Alder Lake-N 8086:462e

message:
The ov5693 never programs MIPI_CTRL00 (0x4800), leaving it at its 0x00
power-on default, which lets the MIPI clock run freely. The IPU3 CSI-2
receiver tolerates this, but the IPU6 receiver (e.g. on Microsoft
Surface Pro 7+, Pro 8, Pro 9 and Surface Go 4) fails to lock onto the
link, so the sensor streams but capture times out with "stream stop
time out". On most affected machines no frames arrive at all; on some
the failure is intermittent.

Gate the clock lane while idle at stream on when the endpoint requests a
non-continuous clock.

Only the gate bit is touched, so platforms that do not request it are
unaffected. No counterpart is needed at stream off, as the link is down
by then and the register returns to its default when the sensor is
powered off.

The property is supplied by the ipu-bridge in a subsequent patch.

author: Fernando Rimoli <fernandorimoli11@gmail.com>
subject: media: ipu-bridge: Request non-continuous clock for ov5693 on IPU6

Tested-by: Jakob Berg Jespersen <dev@berg.pm> # Surface Pro 7+, IPU6 Tiger Lake
Fil Dunsky <filipp.dunsky@gmail.com> # Surface Pro 8, IPU6 Tiger Lake (8086:9a19)

author: Fernando Rimoli <fernandorimoli11@gmail.com>
subject: media: ipu-bridge: Keep the clock-noncontinuous property name out of rodata

Fixes: 8e3def7bf410 ("media: ipu-bridge: Request non-continuous clock for ov5693 on IPU6")

message:
The software nodes ipu-bridge registers on a successful init are never
unregistered. There is no module_exit and no remove hook, and every
software_node_unregister_node_group() call sits on an error unwind label
inside ipu_bridge_init(), so on success the nodes stay registered and
readable after the module is unloaded, which a later rebind relies on.

Nothing reachable from a registered node may therefore point into the
module image. PROPERTY_ENTRY_BOOL() stores a pointer to its name, so the
"clock-noncontinuous" string literal leaves the surviving node carrying a
dangling property name once ipu-bridge is gone.

Add the name to struct ipu_property_names, which is copied by value into
each struct ipu_sensor, and use that copy, as every other endpoint
property name already does.

Fixes: 8e3def7bf410 ("media: ipu-bridge: Request non-continuous clock for ov5693 on IPU6")
Reported-by: D. Manresa <dmanresa@gmail.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-media/20260905211307.542810-1-dmanresa@gmail.com/

author: Sergey Lebedev <lsa.uz@pm.me>
subject: media: i2c: ov13858: add horizontal and vertical flip controls
message:
The Microsoft Surface Pro 11 for Business (Intel) mounts this sensor
upside down, as commit b238116ccd4b ("media: ipu-bridge: Add upside-down
quirk for Surface Pro 11") records, and the driver has no flip controls
to compensate.

Add V4L2_CID_HFLIP and V4L2_CID_VFLIP on bits 3 and 4 of register 0x3820.
The mirror bit is active low, as in Intel's out-of-tree ov13858 driver.
The Bayer order does not change with either flip, so the controls do not
set V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_MODIFY_LAYOUT. They are clustered, and grabbed while
streaming.

author: Fernando Rimoli <fernandorimoli11@gmail.com>
subject: media: ipu-bridge: Add upside-down sensor quirks for the Surface Pro 9
message:
The Microsoft Surface Pro 9 mounts both its front sensor (OVTI5693) and
its rear one (OVTID858) rotated 180 degrees, and its SSDB reports 0 for
each, so frames from either arrive inverted with nothing to say so.

Add both to upside_down_sensor_dmi_ids. The two entries carry identical
DMI matches and differ only in the ACPI HID they gate on, which works
because ipu_bridge_parse_rotation() walks every matching DMI entry rather
than stopping at the first one.

Measured on a Surface Pro 9, DMI product SKU Surface_Pro_9_2038, IPU6
Alder Lake-P 8086:465d, where the inversion of both sensors was confirmed
visually. Matched on DMI_PRODUCT_NAME as the rest of the table is, rather
than on the narrower SKU: the entries only take effect when the ACPI HID
matches too, so a variant of the same model that shipped different
sensors is left alone.

This makes the kernel report the mounting truthfully and does no more
than that. Nothing in the bridge rotates pixels, so an application that
reads the property can turn the image the right way up while one that
ignores it still shows it inverted.

Signed-off-by: Fernando Rimoli <fernandorimoli11@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com>
(cherry picked from commit db44b1792898143888652ea1b54348315eedab4e)
[Backport: context only. 7.3 ends the table with the Samsung 960QHA entry, so the
 two entries go after it, before the terminator.]

author: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
subject: media: ipu-bridge: Drop the Surface Pro 9 front camera quirk superseded upstream

(OVTI5693). The upstream commit db44b1792898 ("media: ipu-bridge: Add
upside-down sensor quirks for the Surface Pro 9"), backported earlier in

(OVTID858) sensor of the same model.

Drop the older front entry, so that each sensor is listed once and the
Surface Pro 9 entries are exactly the ones in mainline from 7.4 on. The
Surface Pro 8 entry is not upstream, and stays.

The upstream entries match the vendor with DMI_EXACT_MATCH where the

subject: HID: Add hid-surface driver to filter BTN_0 (FN key)
message:

as BTN_0 (button 256) through runtime HID events. This button can get
stuck in pressed state, flooding the input system and breaking focus
tracking in KWin Wayland compositor.

Add a new hid-surface driver that filters BTN_0 events using the event
callback. The FN key should be handled as a hardware modifier and not
reported to the OS.

Tested on Surface Laptop 4 AMD with KDE Plasma Wayland. After the fix:
- FN key combinations work correctly (volume, brightness)
- Focus tracking no longer breaks
- Mouse clicks work on all windows

author: Chris Simpson <chris@nilk.net>
subject: ALSA: hda/realtek: Limit internal mic gain on Microsoft Surface Pro 9
message:
The Surface Pro 9 internal mic (ALC274, pin 0x12) has a Mic Boost of
up to +30 dB on top of a Capture volume of up to +30 dB.  User space
that has no saved level for the source starts both at the maximum,
+60 dB, where 37% of the samples clip.  Measured on the device, the
mic is clean at +18 dB, while +30 dB with no boost already reaches
0 dBFS on normal room audio.

Remove the Mic Boost control and limit every ADC to +18 dB, so that
the default 100% source volume is a usable level.

The PCI SSID (8086:7270) and codec SSID (10ec:1284) are Intel and
Realtek defaults, so other machines report them too.  Keep the entry
out of the main table, and pick it from a table of its own, by codec
SSID, only when the main table had no match and the DMI vendor and
product name match.  Every other machine picks its fixups as before.

Assisted-by: LLM
